secondary_filing: 0000004281-24-000026_10-Q.txt (10-Q for Q2 2024, filed 2024-07-30) — used for Q2-2024 forward-looking commentary
notes: Howmet is a Tier-1/2 aerospace components supplier (engine castings, fasteners, structures, titanium mill products, forged wheels). Defense aerospace is ~15% of FY2023 revenue. The 10-K names exactly ONE specific DoD platform/program by name (F-35) and references it in (a) Legal Proceedings (RTI titanium MPO litigation with Lockheed Martin) and (b) Engineered Structures MD&A (year-over-year segment volume commentary). Otherwise the 10-K speaks in aggregate ('defense aerospace', 'commercial transportation', 'industrial gas turbine') without naming PEs, contract numbers, or program-of-record line items. Customer concentration is disclosed in aggregate (GE 12%, RTX 9%) without program attribution. This filing is therefore a LOW-DENSITY J-Book target: few program-specific claims to verify, most exposure is at the platform level (F-35 final-assembly volumes) rather than RDT&E Program Element level.

claims.claim_text: Engineered Structures segment volumes were impacted by lower F-35 program volumes (year-over-year, 2022 -> 2023 and earlier 2021 -> 2022), implying that F-35 production-program demand is a material driver of Engineered Structures' defense aerospace revenue line.
claims.subject: Engineered Structures segment
claims.object_value: F-35 named as the specific defense program cited in segment-level volume commentary
claims.source_quote: Third-party sales for the Engineered Structures segment ... partially offset by lower volumes in the defense aerospace market, including lower F-35 program volumes, and Boeing 787 production declines. ... Segment Adjusted EBITDA for the Engineered Structures segment increased $8, or 8%, in 2022 compared with 2021, primarily due to higher volumes in the narrow body commercial aerospace market and favorable product pricing, partially offset by lower volumes in the defense aerospace market, including lower F-35 program volumes, and Boeing 787 production declines as well as inflationary costs.

claims.claim_text: Howmet's subsidiary RTI Advanced Forming, Inc. is a titanium mill-product supplier to the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter production program via a Master Purchase Order with Lockheed Martin; the company is litigating fair-market price adjustments on F-35 titanium. This means forward F-35 production rates are load-bearing for the Engineered Structures titanium book.
claims.subject: RTI Advanced Forming (Howmet sub)
claims.predicate: supplies titanium mill products to F-35 production via Lockheed Martin MPO
claims.object_value: F-35 Program (Lockheed Martin prime; RTI sub-tier titanium supplier)
claims.source_quote: On November 30, 2023, Lockheed Martin Corporation filed a complaint ... against the Company and its subsidiary RTI Advanced Forming, Inc. ('RTI') as defendants. The complaint alleges that the Company and RTI breached a Master Purchase Order ('MPO') between Lockheed Martin and RTI related to the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter production program between Lockheed Martin and the United States government (the 'F-35 Program') by seeking a fair market price adjustment for the provision of titanium mill products under RTI's separate agreements with Lockheed Martin's subcontractors for the F-35 Program (the 'Qualified Suppliers').

claims.claim_text: Customer concentration: in FY2023, General Electric Company represented approximately 12% and RTX Corporation approximately 9% of Howmet's third-party sales (top-2 customers ~21% of revenue). This is aggregate top-customer disclosure with no program-of-record / PE-level attribution — the customers are commercial engine OEMs whose military pull-through includes F119 (F-22), F135 (F-35), and engine spares.
claims.subject: Howmet third-party sales mix (FY2023)
claims.predicate: concentrated on GE and RTX as top customers
claims.object_value: GE ~12%, RTX ~9% of FY2023 third-party sales (~21% combined)
claims.source_quote: In 2023, General Electric Company and RTX Corporation represented approximately 12% and 9%, respectively, of the Company's third-party sales. The loss of any such significant customer could have a material adverse effect on such businesses.

claims.claim_text: Howmet forward-projects 2024 sales growth from defense aerospace (alongside commercial aerospace, commercial transportation, and industrial markets), with the segment-level outlook saying 'In 2024, management projects sales to increase as we expect solid growth in the commercial aerospace market.' Defense aerospace is named in the segment MD&A but no specific Program Element, PE number, or program-of-record line item is disclosed; the forward defense outlook is grounded in general 'U.S. and foreign government funding.'
claims.subject: Howmet 2024 defense aerospace outlook
claims.object_value: no named PE / program-of-record cited; forward exposure described only at the aggregate 'defense aerospace' market level
claims.source_quote: In 2024, management projects sales to increase as we expect solid growth in the commercial aerospace market, and the Company's strong position in that market is expected to continue. ... The defense aerospace cycle is highly dependent on U.S. and foreign government funding. Reductions in defense spending may affect current and future funding of these programs and could reduce the demand for Howmet's products.

claims.claim_text: Howmet's Engineered Structures segment serves 'commercial aerospace, defense aerospace, and land and sea defense' applications, producing titanium ingots, mill products, forgings, extrusions, and forming/machining for airframe, wing, aero-engine, and landing-gear components. The narrative implies titanium-heavy airframe exposure to military fighters (F-15, F-18, F-22, F-35) but no specific program revenue split is given.
claims.subject: Engineered Structures segment end-markets
claims.predicate: serves multiple defense aerospace and land/sea defense customers
claims.object_value: no specific platform revenue attribution disclosed; titanium mill products exposure inferred to F-35, F-22, F-18, F-15 platforms
claims.source_quote: Engineered Structures produces titanium ingots and mill products for aerospace and defense applications and is vertically integrated to produce titanium forgings, extrusions, forming and machining services for airframe, wing, aero-engine, and landing gear components. ... The principal markets served by Engineered Structures are commercial aerospace, defense aerospace, and land and sea defense.

claims.claim_text: Engine Products segment relies on long-term contracts with engine OEMs (GE Aerospace, RTX Pratt & Whitney, CFM, Rolls-Royce) and identifies 'next-generation engine programs' (commercial: LEAP, GTF, GEnx, GE9X; defense: F135, F119) as drivers — but no specific defense engine PE or production line item is disclosed.
claims.subject: Engine Products segment customer/program structure
claims.predicate: supplies airfoils, castings, rings to commercial + defense aero-engine OEMs
claims.object_value: long-term contracts, no named defense-engine PE or production rate disclosed
claims.source_quote: Engine Products utilizes advanced designs and techniques to support next-generation engine programs and produces components primarily for aircraft engines and industrial gas turbines, including airfoils and seamless rolled rings. ... Engine Products principally serves the commercial and defense aerospace, industrial gas turbine, and oil and gas markets.

claims.claim_text: Defense aerospace was 15% of FY2023 revenue (down from 19% in FY2021, 16% in FY2022) — i.e., the defense mix is SHRINKING as a share of the company as commercial aerospace recovers. Forward-looking statements caveat that 'changes in military strategy, policy and priorities, or reductions in defense spending, may affect current and future funding of these programs.'

claims.source_quote: Aerospace - Commercial 49% 46% 41% Aerospace - Defense 15% 16% 19% Commercial Transportation 21% 23% 23% Industrial and Other 15% 15% 17% ... The defense aerospace cycle is highly dependent on U.S. and foreign government funding. ... reductions in defense spending, may affect current and future funding of these programs and could reduce the demand for Howmet's products.

claims.claim_text: Patent portfolio: 'As of the end of 2023, the Company's worldwide patent portfolio consists of approximately 940 granted patents and 215 pending patent applications.' Howmet describes patents/trade secrets as a competitive advantage but explicitly states the business is NOT materially dependent on any single patent — i.e., patent claim is supportable in aggregate but not a single-PE narrative.
claims.subject: Howmet patent portfolio
claims.source_quote: As of the end of 2023, the Company's worldwide patent portfolio consists of approximately 940 granted patents and 215 pending patent applications. ... Howmet's business as a whole is not, however, materially dependent on any single patent, trade secret or trademark.

claims.claim_text: Howmet operates ~50 principal facilities worldwide across 20 countries with ~23,200 employees as of YE 2023; specific U.S. plants include Whitehall MI (UAW, ~1,400 employees), Cleveland OH (UAW, ~750), Savannah GA, La Porte IN, Wichita Falls TX, Hampton VA, Dover NJ. This is a verifiable physical-footprint claim independent of the J-Book.

claims.source_quote: Total worldwide employment at the end of 2023 was approximately 23,200 employees in 23 countries. ...
